Rodrigo, we need to choose a vanilla supplier for next year. What do you think?
I compared the two. The supplier in Indonesia is cheaper than the supplier in Madagascar.
How much cheaper?
About twelve percent. But Madagascar is more reliable. Their deliveries are never late.
That's important. And which one is faster?
Indonesia is faster: twenty days, not thirty-five. But the quality from Madagascar is better.
I see. And our stock in Brazil? Is it better than last quarter?
Yes, it is higher. We have stock for three months now. Last quarter we had only six weeks.
Good. So my question is: for us, is cheaper better, or is reliable better?
For vanilla, reliable is better. Madagascar is more expensive, but a late delivery is more expensive for the client.

Hello, Mister Luiz, this is David Chen from Java Aromatics, in Jakarta. Thank you for your e-mail. About our price: this year our vanilla is ten percent cheaper than last year. And our delivery is faster now, only twenty days to Santos. We have a new warehouse, bigger than the old one, so our stock is always ready. I can send you a sample this week. Please call me back when you can. Thank you.

Hi Rodrigo, it is Claire. I have the numbers for the third quarter. Brazil is better than in the second quarter: the cost is lower, and the deliveries are faster. Mexico is also good, but their stock is lower than yours. Only one number is worse: the price of transport. It is more expensive than last year, in all the regions. Can we talk about it on Monday? Thanks.

Claire asked Rodrigo to compare two vanilla suppliers. He looked at the prices, and the supplier in Indonesia was cheaper. Then he looked at the deliveries, and Madagascar was more reliable. He also saw that the quality from Madagascar was better. In the end he chose Madagascar, the more expensive supplier.
